name: Samsung
summary: Samsung hires engineers across its electronics businesses and research centres, including Samsung R&D Institute India-Bangalore, which Samsung describes as its largest R&D centre outside South Korea. Candidates commonly report an online coding test for software roles that rewards fully working solutions, then technical interviews on data structures, operating systems and projects, and an HR round. Samsung publishes five core values: People, Excellence, Change, Integrity and Co-prosperity.
rounds: Online coding test for software roles; candidates commonly report it rewards fully correct, well-tested solutions
Technical screening in digital electronics or your stream for some hardware and VLSI roles
One or two technical interviews: data structures, algorithms, operating systems, networks and your projects
For experienced roles, a deeper interview on the team's domain, such as Android, multimedia, modem, AI or chip design
HR round on motivation and teamwork
looks_for: Correct, working code and careful handling of edge cases
Solid computer science or electronics fundamentals
Depth in the team's domain: Android, multimedia, networks, AI or chip design

questions.text: Tell me about a time you kept improving something that already worked because you knew it could be better.
covers: What 'working' looked like and what still fell short
What you improved and how you measured it
Whether the extra effort paid off

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to adapt quickly to a big change in a project.
covers: What changed and how it affected your plan
How you re-planned and kept the team moving
The outcome and what you learned about handling change

questions.text: Tell me about a time you worked with people from another country or culture on a shared goal.
covers: The goal and the differences you had to work across: language, time zones, styles
What you did to communicate clearly and build trust
What was delivered and what you'd do differently

questions.text: Tell me about a time you submitted work with a bug you'd missed. What did you change in how you test?
covers: The bug and why you missed it
How you fixed it and owned it
The testing habit you've built since

questions.text: How do you make sure your code handles edge cases before you submit it in a timed coding test?
covers: Reading the constraints carefully and listing edge cases: empty, smallest, largest, repeated values
Dry-running the logic by hand on a small example
Writing your own test inputs, including worst-case sizes for speed

questions.text: Explain BFS and DFS, and describe a situation where you'd pick each.
covers: Level-by-level search with a queue versus going deep with a stack or recursion
BFS for shortest paths in unweighted graphs; DFS for exploring all options or detecting cycles
Memory use and the risk of deep recursion

questions.text: Explain virtual memory and paging, and what happens on a page fault.
covers: Each process sees its own address space, mapped to physical memory by page tables
The TLB and why it matters for speed
A page fault: the OS loads the page or stops the process if the access is invalid

questions.text: Explain how an Android app's activity lifecycle works, and describe a bug that comes from handling it badly.
covers: The main states: created, started, resumed, paused, stopped, destroyed
What to save and release at each step
A typical bug, such as lost data on screen rotation or a leak from a held reference

questions.text: How would you reduce the battery drain of a feature that runs in the background on a phone?
covers: Measuring first: wake-ups, network use, location and sensor use
Batching work, using system schedulers, and doing less when the battery is low
Checking the feature still works well enough for users

questions.text: How would you design the software update system for millions of TVs or phones so a bad update can't break them all?
covers: Staged rollouts with monitoring and a pause button
Verifying update packages and keeping a fallback copy of the old version on the device
Handling poor connections, low storage and devices that are switched off

questions.text: What is a memory leak in C or C++, and how would you find one in a device that runs for weeks?
covers: Memory allocated and never freed, growing until the device slows or crashes
Finding it: tracking memory over time, leak-detection tools, allocation logs
Preventing it: clear ownership, RAII and smart pointers

questions.text: How would you design a smart-home system that lets a phone control appliances from different makers?
covers: A device model that describes what each appliance can do
Local control through a hub plus cloud control, and support for common standards
Security, pairing new devices, and what still works offline

questions.text: Explain the difference between a latch and a flip-flop, and why designs usually prefer flip-flops.
covers: Level-sensitive latches versus edge-triggered flip-flops
Why flip-flops make timing analysis simpler and more predictable
Where latches are still used, such as some low-power or high-speed designs

questions.text: Tell me about yourself and your strongest technical project.
covers: Your background in a few sentences
One project, the code or design you did yourself, and its result
Why it makes you a fit for this role

questions.text: Why Samsung, and which product or research area would you like to work on?
covers: A specific product or research area, such as phones, TVs, smart home, chips or AI
A link to your skills or projects
What you'd want to build or learn

tips: Practise solving one hard problem completely in a timed setting, with your own test cases; candidates commonly report that partial solutions score poorly.
For software tests, revise graph search, recursion with backtracking and simulation-style problems, which candidates often mention.
Know the product side, from Galaxy phones and TVs to SmartThings and semiconductors, and connect your interest to one area.
Samsung lists five core values, including Excellence and Co-prosperity; have a story about teamwork and one about improving quality.
Prepare to explain your projects in depth, especially the code you wrote yourself.

sources.title: Samsung Careers: life at Samsung (core values)
